1	# AI Persona Builder
     2	
     3	Build AI persona instruction files for **VS Code Chat**, **Claude Code** and **LangGraph Deep Agents** from YAML metadata and Markdown templates — with zero configuration friction.
     4	
     5	Define your personas once as simple YAML + Markdown sources, and the library generates correctly formatted instruction files for both IDEs. A plugin system lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or post-process output without touching the core engine.
     6	
     7	## ✨ Features
     8	
     9	- **Multi-target output** — generates VS Code `.agent.md`, Claude Code `.md`, Deep Agents `.md`, and any custom format from a single source
    10	- **Extensible target registry** — register custom targets via `TargetRegistry` without touching core code; each target declares its own output key, frontmatter template, and context flags
    11	- **YAML + Markdown templating** — separate metadata from content; merge them at build time with `{{variables}}`, `{{> partials}}`, and `{{#if}}` conditionals
    12	- **Shared + per-suite partials** — reuse content fragments across personas with local overrides
    13	- **Plugin architecture** — hook into context building, post-rendering, validation, and frontmatter generation
    14	- **CI-friendly** — `--check` mode renders without writing; `--strict` exits non-zero on warnings
    15	- **Programmatic & CLI** — use the `build()` API in scripts or run `persona-build` from the command line
    16	- **Single dependency** — only `js-yaml` at runtime
    17	
    18	## 📋 Requirements
    19	
    20	- **Node.js** ≥ 18
    21	
    22	## 🚀 Quick Start
    23	
    24	```bash
    25	npm install @mistralys/persona-builder
    26	```
    27	
    28	- View on NPM: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mistralys/persona-builder
    29	- View on Github: https://github.com/Mistralys/ai-persona-builder
    30	
    31	### Programmatic API
    32	
    33	```ts
    34	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    35	import path from 'node:path';
    36	
    37	const summary = await build({
    38	  suites: {
    39	    'my-suite': {
    40	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
    41	      outputDirs: {
    42	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
    43	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
    44	      },
    45	    },
    46	  },
    47	  sharedPartialsDir: path.resolve('./personas/shared/partials'),
    48	});
    49	
    50	console.log(`Built ${summary.totalBuilt} persona(s), wrote ${summary.totalWritten} file(s).`);
    51	```
    52	
    53	### CLI
    54	
    55	```bash
    56	# Create a persona-build.config.js, then:
    57	npx persona-build
    58	
    59	# CI staleness check
    60	npx persona-build --check --strict
    61	```
    62	
    63	See the [CLI docs](docs/cli.md) for config file format and all flags.
    64	
    65	## 📖 Documentation
    66	
    67	**Guides** — conceptual and procedural reading:
    68	
    69	| Guide | Description |
    70	|-------|-------------|
    71	| [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) | Step-by-step tutorial — build your first persona from scratch |
    72	| [Directory Convention](docs/directory-convention.md) | Expected source layout (`meta/`, `content/`, `partials/`) |
    73	| [Template Syntax](docs/template-syntax.md) | Variables, partials, conditionals, and built-in context variables |
    74	| [Plugins](docs/plugins.md) | `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface and examples |
    75	
    76	**Reference** — look-up material:
    77	
    78	| Reference | Description |
    79	|-----------|-------------|
    80	| [Metadata Reference](docs/metadata-reference.md) | All recognized YAML metadata fields, tiers, and fallback rules |
    81	| [Configuration Reference](docs/configuration.md) | `BuildConfig`, `SuiteConfig`, and `BuildSummary` fields |
    82	| [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Command-line flags, config file format, and common patterns |
    83	| [Public API](docs/api.md) | All exported types and functions |
    84	| [Project Manifest](docs/agents/project-manifest/README.md) | Canonical documentation for AI agent sessions |
    85	
    86	## 🔌 Plugins
    87	
    88	The library ships with a plugin system that lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or
    89	post-process output without touching the core engine. See [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) for
    90	the `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface, examples, and the available hooks.
    91	
    92	> **Ledger plugin:** The first-party ledger plugin was migrated out of this library in v2.0.0 and
    93	> is now maintained in the [ai-insights](https://github.com/mistralys/ai-insights-dev) workspace.
    94	> The `@mistralys/persona-builder/plugins/ledger` sub-path export no longer exists.
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## 📄 License
    99	
   100	MIT

1	# Plugins
     2	
     3	Plugins extend the build pipeline without modifying the core engine. Register plugins via `BuildConfig.plugins`.
     4	
     5	## PersonaBuildPlugin Interface
     6	
     7	Hook invocation order per persona:
     8	
     9	1. `onSuiteInit`      — once per suite, before any persona is built
    10	2. `onPartials`       — once per suite, after partials are loaded from disk
    11	3. `onBuildContext`   — per persona, before template rendering
    12	4. `onPersonaPartials` — per persona, before template rendering (after `onBuildContext`)
    13	5. `onPostRender`     — per persona, after body rendering
    14	6. `onValidate`       — per persona, during the validation phase
    15	
    16	```ts
    17	interface PersonaBuildPlugin {
    18	  /** Unique name used for logging and identification */
    19	  name: string;
    20	
    21	  /**
    22	   * Called once per suite before any persona is built.
    23	   * Use this to read shared metadata and set up plugin state.
    24	   */
    25	  onSuiteInit?(suite: SuiteConfig, sharedMeta: Record<string, unknown>): void;
    26	
    27	  /**
    28	   * Called once per suite after partials are loaded from disk (after any
    29	   * BuildConfig.partials inline map has been applied), but before any persona
    30	   * is rendered.
    31	   *
    32	   * Plugins are chained: each plugin receives the accumulated partials map
    33	   * returned by the previous plugin. Return the (possibly mutated or extended)
    34	   * map to pass it to the next plugin. The returned map must include all
    35	   * original keys.
    36	   */
    37	  onPartials?(
    38	    partialsMap: Record<string, string>,
    39	    suiteName: string,
    40	    suite: SuiteConfig,
    41	  ): Record<string, string>;
    42	
    43	  /**
    44	   * Called for each persona before template rendering.
    45	   * Mutate and return the context to inject additional template variables.
    46	   * The optional `target` parameter indicates the active build target.
    47	   */
    48	  onBuildContext?(
    49	    context: Record<string, unknown>,
    50	    persona: PersonaMetadata,
    51	    suite: SuiteConfig,
    52	    target?: TargetType,
    53	  ): Record<string, unknown>;
    54	
    55	  /**
    56	   * Called for each persona (and target) after `onBuildContext`, before
    57	   * template rendering.
    58	   *
    59	   * Allows plugins to inject or override partials on a per-persona basis.
    60	   * Plugins are chained: each plugin receives the accumulated partials map
    61	   * returned by the previous plugin. Return the (possibly mutated or extended)
    62	   * map to pass it to the next plugin. The returned map must include all
    63	   * original keys.
    64	   *
    65	   * **Isolation guarantee:** The builder shallow-copies the suite-level partials
    66	   * map before the first plugin in the chain is called. The `partialsMap` you
    67	   * receive is already persona-scoped — changes applied here are invisible to
    68	   * other personas in the same suite. Do **not** mutate `partialsMap` in place;
    69	   * return a new map instead (e.g. `{ ...partialsMap, myPartial: '...' }`).
    70	   *
    71	   * The `context` parameter reflects the post-`onBuildContext` state: persona
    72	   * metadata and any keys injected by earlier `onBuildContext` plugins are
    73	   * accessible, so you can make partial content conditional on persona fields.
    74	   */
    75	  onPersonaPartials?(
    76	    partialsMap: Record<string, string>,
    77	    persona: PersonaMetadata,
    78	    context: Record<string, unknown>,
    79	    suite: SuiteConfig,
    80	    target?: TargetType,
    81	  ): Record<string, string>;
    82	
    83	  /**
    84	   * Called after the full output is rendered.
    85	   * Mutate and return the output string (e.g. to append a footer).
    86	   */
    87	  onPostRender?(output: string, persona: PersonaMetadata, target: TargetType): string;
    88	
    89	  /**
    90	   * Called during the validation phase.
    91	   * Return an array of ValidationResult entries (empty = no issues).
    92	   */
    93	  onValidate?(persona: PersonaMetadata, suite: SuiteConfig, target?: TargetType): ValidationResult[];
    94	
    95	  /**
    96	   * Register custom frontmatter templates, keyed by target type.
    97	   * These override the library defaults and config-level overrides.
    98	   */
    99	  frontmatterTemplates?: Partial<Record<TargetType, string>>;
   100	}

1	# Configuration Reference
     2	
     3	## BuildConfig
     4	
     5	The configuration object passed to `build()`.
     6	
     7	| Field | Type | Default | Description |
     8	|-------|------|---------|-------------|
     9	| `suites` | `Record<string, SuiteConfig>` | **required** | Map of suite names to suite configurations. |
    10	| `sharedPartialsDir` | `string` | `undefined` | Absolute path to a shared partials directory. Forms the **middle** layer in partial resolution: `BuildConfig.partials` (lowest) → `sharedPartialsDir` → suite-local partials (highest). |
    11	| `partials` | `Record<string, string>` | `undefined` | Inline partials map (partial name → content). Forms the **lowest** layer in partial resolution: `BuildConfig.partials` (lowest) → `sharedPartialsDir` → suite-local partials (highest). Useful for injecting programmatically generated content without touching the filesystem. |
    12	| `variables` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `undefined` | Global template variables available to every persona during rendering. Forms layer 1 (lowest priority) of the 7-layer merge chain: `BuildConfig.variables` → `SuiteConfig.variables` → `_shared.yaml` → per-persona YAML → derived fields → agent map → target flags. Suite-level `SuiteConfig.variables` are merged on top of these and take precedence when the same key appears in both. |
    13	| `plugins` | `PersonaBuildPlugin[]` | `[]` | Plugins applied to every suite in registration order. |
    14	| `targets` | `string[]` | See below | Output targets to generate. The default is derived from the registry: all targets where `defaultEnabled !== false`. For `defaultRegistry`, this yields `['vscode', 'claude-code']` (the `'deep-agents'` target has `defaultEnabled: false`). Pass an explicit array to override. |
    15	| `check` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, personas are rendered but **no files are written**. Useful for CI staleness checks. |
    16	| `strict` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, the build throws if any `ValidationResult` has severity `'error'` or `'warning'`. |
    17	| `frontmatter` | `Record<string, string>` | Registry defaults | Override the default frontmatter templates, keyed by target name. See [template syntax](template-syntax.md). |
    18	| `targetRegistry` | `TargetRegistry` | `defaultRegistry` | Registry of target definitions to use for this build. When provided, overrides `defaultRegistry` for output directory resolution, filename lookup, frontmatter defaults, and context flag injection. Register custom targets here to extend the build system. |
    19	
    20	## SuiteConfig
    21	
    22	Per-suite configuration nested inside `BuildConfig.suites`.
    23	
    24	| Field | Type | Default | Description |
    25	|-------|------|---------|-------------|
    26	| `srcDir` | `string` | **required** | Absolute or relative path to the suite source directory. |
    27	| `outVscode` | `string` | `undefined` | _(Deprecated)_ Output directory for VS Code persona files. Use `outputDirs['vscode']` instead; that takes precedence when present. Will be removed in a future major version. |
    28	| `outClaudeCode` | `string` | `undefined` | _(Deprecated)_ Output directory for Claude Code persona files. Use `outputDirs['claude-code']` instead; that takes precedence when present. Will be removed in a future major version. |
    29	| `outputDirs` | `Record<string, string>` | `undefined` | Map of output directories keyed by each target's `outputDirKey` (see note below). Takes precedence over the deprecated fields. Required for the `'deep-agents'` built-in and all custom targets. |
    30	| `personaMode` | `string` | `undefined` | Passthrough value exposed to plugins. The core library does nothing with it; its meaning is entirely plugin-defined. Use it to vary plugin behaviour per suite (e.g. apply different rendering logic when `personaMode === 'ledger'` vs `personaMode === 'standalone'`). Plugins can read it inside `onSuiteInit` and `onBuildContext` via `suite.personaMode`. |
    31	| `partialsSubdir` | `string` | `'partials'` | Sub-directory within `srcDir` containing suite-local partials. |
    32	| `metaSubdir` | `string` | `'meta'` | Sub-directory within `srcDir` containing YAML metadata files. |
    33	| `contentSubdir` | `string` | `'content'` | Sub-directory within `srcDir` containing Markdown content templates. |
    34	| `variables` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `undefined` | Suite-level template variables. Forms layer 2 of the 7-layer merge chain: `BuildConfig.variables` → `SuiteConfig.variables` → `_shared.yaml` → per-persona YAML → derived fields → agent map → target flags. Overrides `BuildConfig.variables` for the same key; itself overridden by `_shared.yaml` and per-persona YAML fields. |
    35	
    36	> **`outputDirs` key note:** Each key in `outputDirs` must match the target's `outputDirKey` field (declared in its `TargetDefinition`), **not** necessarily the target name. For the three built-in targets `outputDirKey` equals the target name (`'vscode'`, `'claude-code'`, `'deep-agents'`), so there is no difference in practice. For a custom target where `outputDirKey` differs from `name`, use the `outputDirKey` value as the map key.
    37	
    38	## BuildSummary
    39	
    40	The object returned by `build()`.
    41	
    42	| Field | Type | Description |
    43	|-------|------|-------------|
    44	| `success` | `boolean` | `true` unless strict mode is on and there are validation failures. |
    45	| `results` | `BuildResult[]` | One entry per persona × target combination. |
    46	| `strictFailures` | `ValidationResult[]` | Validation issues that triggered a strict-mode failure. |
    47	| `totalBuilt` | `number` | Total number of persona × target combinations processed. |
    48	| `totalWritten` | `number` | Number of output files actually written to disk (0 in check mode). |

1	# Getting Started
     2	
     3	> Output verified against `@mistralys/persona-builder` v2.1.x.
     4	
     5	This tutorial walks through building your first pair of VS Code and Claude Code persona files
     6	from scratch. You will end up with two ready-to-use instruction files generated from a single
     7	source.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## 1. Install the package
    12	
    13	```bash
    14	npm install @mistralys/persona-builder
    15	```
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## 2. Create the directory structure
    20	
    21	Personas live inside a **suite directory**. Each suite has three sub-directories:
    22	
    23	```
    24	my-project/
    25	├── persona-build.config.js
    26	├── personas/
    27	│   ├── shared/
    28	│   │   └── partials/               # Cross-suite reusable fragments
    29	│   │       └── greeting.md
    30	│   └── my-suite/                   # Suite source directory (srcDir)
    31	│       ├── meta/
    32	│       │   ├── _shared.yaml        # Suite-wide defaults
    33	│       │   └── code-reviewer.yaml  # Per-persona metadata
    34	│       ├── content/
    35	│       │   └── code-reviewer.md    # Markdown content template
    36	│       └── partials/               # Suite-local reusable fragments
    37	│           └── footer.md
    38	└── dist/
    39	    ├── vscode/                     # Generated VS Code output
    40	    └── claude-code/                # Generated Claude Code output
    41	```
    42	
    43	---
    44	
    45	## 3. Write the shared partial
    46	
    47	**`personas/shared/partials/greeting.md`**
    48	
    49	```md
    50	Hello, I am {{name}} v{{version}}.
    51	```
    52	
    53	This partial will be included anywhere a template writes `{{> greeting}}`. Variable
    54	substitution (`{{name}}`, `{{version}}`) happens after partial resolution, so the partial
    55	can reference any context variable.
    56	
    57	---
    58	
    59	## 4. Write the suite-local partial
    60	
    61	**`personas/my-suite/partials/footer.md`**
    62	
    63	```md
    64	*Generated by AI Persona Builder.*
    65	```
    66	
    67	Suite-local partials override shared partials with the same stem name. They are only
    68	available inside the suite that defines them.
    69	
    70	> **Partials resolution order (four layers):**
    71	> 1. `BuildConfig.partials` — inline partial map (lowest precedence)
    72	> 2. `sharedPartialsDir` — shared cross-suite partials loaded from disk
    73	> 3. Suite-local partials — files in `<srcDir>/partials/` (this directory)
    74	> 4. `onPartials` plugin hooks — plugin-injected partials (highest precedence, always win)
    75	
    76	---
    77	
    78	## 5. Write the shared defaults
    79	
    80	**`personas/my-suite/meta/_shared.yaml`**
    81	
    82	```yaml
    83	default_version: '1.0.0'
    84	author: Your Name
    85	cc_permission_mode: default
    86	cc_model: claude-sonnet-4-5
    87	cc_memory: project
    88	```
    89	
    90	Every persona in the suite inherits these values unless a per-persona file overrides them.
    91	The `cc_*` fields are required by the default Claude Code frontmatter template. Set them
    92	here once so every persona in the suite picks them up automatically.
    93	
    94	See [Metadata Reference → Shared Defaults](metadata-reference.md#shared-defaults--meta_sharedyaml)
    95	for the full list of recognized `_shared.yaml` fields.

1	# Template Syntax
     2	
     3	Templates use a lightweight `{{…}}` syntax with no external dependencies.
     4	
     5	## Variables
     6	
     7	```
     8	{{variableName}}
     9	```
    10	
    11	Values are sourced from the merged context built in this priority order (later layers win):
    12	
    13	1. `BuildConfig.variables` — global defaults set in your top-level config
    14	2. `SuiteConfig.variables` — suite-level overrides
    15	3. `_shared.yaml` fields
    16	4. Per-persona YAML fields
    17	5. Derived/computed fields (e.g. `version`, `tools_list`)
    18	6. Cross-suite agent map (`agent_<slug>` variables)
    19	7. Target flags (`target_<name>` booleans) — always highest priority
    20	
    21	Plugin `onBuildContext` hooks run after step 4 and may contribute additional keys or override existing ones. Missing variables emit a warning to stderr but do not fail the build.
    22	
    23	## Partials
    24	
    25	```
    26	{{> partialName}}
    27	```
    28	
    29	Partials are loaded from the `partials/` directory and resolved up to 2 levels deep.
    30	
    31	## Conditionals
    32	
    33	```
    34	{{#if flagName}}
    35	Content shown when flagName is truthy.
    36	{{else}}
    37	Fallback content.
    38	{{/if}}
    39	```
    40	
    41	### Else-If Chains
    42	
    43	Use `{{else if flagName}}` to express multi-branch conditionals without deep nesting:
    44	
    45	```
    46	{{#if a}}
    47	Content shown when a is truthy.
    48	{{else if b}}
    49	Content shown when a is falsy and b is truthy.
    50	{{else}}
    51	Fallback content when both a and b are falsy.
    52	{{/if}}
    53	```
    54	
    55	**Truth table:**
    56	
    57	| `a` | `b` | Output |
    58	|-----|-----|--------|
    59	| `true` | any | first branch |
    60	| `false` | `true` | second branch |
    61	| `false` | `false` | `{{else}}` fallback |
    62	
    63	Chains may have any number of `{{else if}}` branches. The first truthy branch wins;
    64	all subsequent branches are discarded. If no branch is truthy and there is no
    65	`{{else}}`, the entire block is removed from the output.
    66	
    67	`{{else if}}` chains are normalised into equivalent nested `{{#if}}` blocks before
    68	resolution, so they compose correctly with traditional nested syntax.
    69	
    70	### Nested Conditionals
    71	
    72	`{{#if}}` blocks may be nested inside `{{else}}` branches. This is the standard pattern
    73	for writing content that differs across all three built-in targets:
    74	
    75	```
    76	{{#if target_vscode}}
    77	Content shown only in VS Code builds.
    78	{{else}}
    79	{{#if target_deep_agents}}
    80	Content shown only in Deep Agents builds.
    81	{{else}}
    82	Content shown in Claude Code (or any remaining) builds.
    83	{{/if}}
    84	{{/if}}
    85	```
    86	
    87	The engine resolves nested blocks innermost-first across multiple passes until the output
    88	stabilises. No stray `{{/if}}` markers appear in the output regardless of nesting depth.
    89	
    90	## Built-in Context Variables
    91	
    92	The builder automatically derives several convenience variables from YAML metadata:
    93	
    94	| Variable | Source |
    95	|----------|--------|
    96	| `{{version}}` | `version` field, or `default_version` from `_shared.yaml`, or `'0.0.0'` |
    97	| `{{tools_list}}` | Comma-separated string of `tools` array items |
    98	| `{{tools_json}}` | JSON array string of `tools` items |
    99	| `{{cc_tools_list}}` | Comma-separated string of `cc_tools` (falls back to `tools`) |

   260	 * @returns                Merged rendering context

   262	function buildContext(
   263	  personaMeta: Record<string, unknown>,
   264	  sharedMeta: Record<string, unknown>,
   265	  agentMap: Record<string, string> = {},
   266	  target?: TargetType,
   267	  registry?: TargetRegistry,
   268	  configVariables?: Record<string, unknown>,
   269	  suiteVariables?: Record<string, unknown>,

   272	    typeof personaMeta['version'] === 'string'
   273	      ? personaMeta['version']
   274	      : typeof sharedMeta['default_version'] === 'string'
   275	        ? sharedMeta['default_version']
   276	        : '0.0.0';

   278	  // Merge base: configVariables first (lowest priority), then suiteVariables,
   279	  // then sharedMeta, then personaMeta (highest priority among YAML sources).
   280	  const merged: Record<string, unknown> = {
   281	    ...(configVariables ?? {}),
   282	    ...(suiteVariables ?? {}),
   283	    ...sharedMeta,
   284	    ...personaMeta,
   285	    version,
   286	  };

   326	    }

1	# AI Persona Builder
     2	
     3	Build AI persona instruction files for **VS Code Chat**, **Claude Code** and **LangGraph Deep Agents** from YAML metadata and Markdown templates — with zero configuration friction.
     4	
     5	Define your personas once as simple YAML + Markdown sources, and the library generates correctly formatted instruction files for both IDEs. A plugin system lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or post-process output without touching the core engine.
     6	
     7	## ✨ Features
     8	
     9	- **Multi-target output** — generates VS Code `.agent.md`, Claude Code `.md`, Deep Agents `.md`, and any custom format from a single source
    10	- **Extensible target registry** — register custom targets via `TargetRegistry` without touching core code; each target declares its own output key, frontmatter template, and context flags
    11	- **YAML + Markdown templating** — separate metadata from content; merge them at build time with `{{variables}}`, `{{> partials}}`, and `{{#if}}` conditionals
    12	- **Shared + per-suite partials** — reuse content fragments across personas with local overrides
    13	- **Custom variables** — inject global or per-suite template variables via `BuildConfig.variables` and `SuiteConfig.variables` without touching persona YAML files
    14	- **Dynamic partials** — supply inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`, or override them at suite or per-persona level through the `onPartials` and `onPersonaPartials` plugin hooks
    15	- **Plugin architecture** — hook into context building, post-rendering, validation, and frontmatter generation
    16	- **CI-friendly** — `--check` mode renders without writing; `--strict` exits non-zero on warnings
    17	- **Programmatic & CLI** — use the `build()` API in scripts or run `persona-build` from the command line
    18	- **Single dependency** — only `js-yaml` at runtime
